newsitem.title: USA: Oregon House reaches $9.7 bln budget agreement.
newsitem.headline: Oregon House reaches $9.7 bln budget agreement.

text.p: The Oregon House has reached a $9.7 billion budget accord for the 1997-1999 biennium, with $4.2 billion earmarked for schools, Republican House Speaker Lynn Lundquist said on Thursday.

The House budget agreement was reached following bipartisan negotiations, but it still must be put to a vote. The House could vote on the spending plan by June 3, officials said. The state Senate would then review the measure.

The House plan does not use so-called "kicker" funding, or money obtained from tax revenues that exceeded state revenue estimates. Under Oregon law, these funds are supposed to be returned to the taxpayers.
The House budget would allow the state to raise an additional $150 million for schools through the sale of lottery-backed bonds.
The House spending plan was larger than the Senate's $9.5 billion budget, which allocated $4.1 billion for education.
Margaret Hunt, Lundquist's chief of staff, said the speaker was confident of winning House support for the budget compromise.
